clue.text: Work in theatre before away match

parts.note: a play is a work staged in a theatre
off means away, as in 'he's off today'

explanation.surface: A theatre production is staged before the team's away fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A play-off is a deciding contest held to settle a tie, so it is a kind of match.

clue.text: Flap film director's offspring put outside under grass

parts.note: panic grass is a genus of grasses, often just called panic

indicators.note: the offspring are placed around the director's name, enclosing it

parts.note: sons are offspring
Jacques Tati was a French film director

explanation.surface: A movie maker's children are sent outdoors to play on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places the director-in-sons part below the grass in this down entry; Tati is the director of Monsieur Hulot films.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is a state of agitation, which is what a state of alarm and frantic preparation amounts to.

clue.text: Wrong name is put up -— a consequence of this?

definitions.text: Wrong name is put up -— a consequence of this?

indicators.note: something wrong is incorrect or out of order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged
in a down entry, putting up a word reads it from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Calling someone by the wrong name might be a sign of forgetfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NAME gives AMNE, IS put up gives SI, then A; the whole clue then wryly suggests that getting a name wrong is a symptom of memory loss.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory leads people to misname others, so the clue as a whole describes the condition.

clue.text: Perhaps a diamond ring picked up last

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a diamond is perhaps a gem, an example of one
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A diamond engagement ring is collected from the jeweller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks diamond as an example of a gem; the whole run of A, GEM and O is turned to read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence a byword for the last of anything.

clue.text: A number having head of ranch up repeatedly for rustling

indicators.note: repeatedly says the piece built so far is written twice in a row
in a down entry, moving a letter up shifts it nearer the top of the word

parts.note: four is a number

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Cattle rustlers keep returning to the ranch, led by its foreman.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of FOUR (the same letter that heads 'ranch') moves up to second place, giving FROU, then 'repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Frou-frou is the swishing, rustling sound of silk skirts, a direct synonym.

clue.text: With nothing that marks the spot, stay out of sight in neat cover

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
X marks the spot, as on a treasure map
to hide is to stay out of sight

explanation.surface: Someone lies low under a tidy blanket, with no X to betray the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, so neat cover is a cow's skin, not a tidy covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means cattle, and an ox's hide is the covering of such an animal.

clue.text: Strange, young Dombey fixing betting price?

parts.note: odd means strange
the son in Dickens's novel Dombey and Son

explanation.surface: Someone fixes the betting odds on an odd young Dickens character.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds-on is a bookmaker's price for a likely winner, where the stake exceeds the potential return.

clue.text: Like Erica embracing new form of paganism

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heather, so like Erica means heathery

explanation.surface: A woman named Erica takes up a novel kind of pagan worship.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica looks like a woman's name but is the genus of heathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathenry is the condition or practice of heathens, a term for non-Christian belief systems.

clue.text: Female police officer absorbing old traditions

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the officer's letters surround the rest

parts.note: DS is a detective sergeant
lore is a body of traditions

explanation.surface: A policewoman is absorbed in studying ancient customs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolores is a girl's name, so it defines a female by example.

clue.text: Coinage found in chapel environment — not lire

parts.note: a chapel is a nonconformist place of worship, not of the Church of England, so non-C of E

indicators.note: not says a letter is to be dropped from the word it governs

parts.note: one's world is one's environment
L is the abbreviation for lire, Italian currency

explanation.surface: An old coin turns up in the surroundings of a chapel, though it isn't Italian money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coinage' sounds like money, matching 'lire', but means a newly coined word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonce word is one made up for a single occasion, a coinage in the linguistic sense.

clue.text: Incomplete draft lawyer rejected at pleasure

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the combined letters are read backwards
incomplete says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a bill is a draft of a proposed law
DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer turns down an unfinished draft of a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' drops a final letter and 'rejected' then turns the whole run round, giving BILDA backwards; DA is the American term for a prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad lib means freely, at one's pleasure, from the Latin ad libitum.

clue.text: More than blench, accepting article's outrageous

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the article goes inside the run of other letters

parts.note: beyond means more than, as in beyond measure
to blench is to turn white, or pale
the is the definite article; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Something so shocking that it would make anyone go white.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond the pale is an idiom for conduct outside acceptable bounds, that is, outrageous.

clue.text: Conspirator succeeded, protected by accountants

indicators.note: protected by means surrounded, so the letter sits inside the others

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, so two of them give CACA
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A plotter who made it is shielded by his bookkeepers.
explanation.definitionFit: Casca was one of the conspirators who killed Julius Caesar, the first to strike in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: After dope a writer becomes reckless

indicators.note: the writer is placed after the dope in the answer

parts.note: a dope is a fool
Thomas Hardy, the English novelist

explanation.surface: A writer turns reckless after taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs but means an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means rashly bold, a synonym of reckless.

clue.text: A post one mishandled, being a stirrer

indicators.note: mishandled means dealt with badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A post office worker bungles a delivery and causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirrer' suggests a troublemaker, but it is a small spoon for stirring tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoon is used to stir tea or coffee, making it literally a stirrer.

clue.text: Sadness of girl supporting circle in Tamworth

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath
in places the circle inside the animal

parts.note: Tamworth is a British breed of pig
O is circular
Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from the town of Tamworth is upset about her social circle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth looks like the Staffordshire town but is a breed of ginger pig.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignancy is the quality of evoking sadness or deep emotion.

clue.text: Where should I study after school, Dad? We get agreement

parts.words: Where should I study after school
parts.note: a university, uni for short, is where one studies after school
the one asking 'Dad?' is a son

explanation.surface: A child asks their father about university and they find common ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is put by the child, so the speaker addressing Dad supplies SON.
explanation.definitionFit: In unison means in agreement, all acting or speaking together.

clue.text: He discovered certain rays — not green, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physicist laments that his rays did not turn out green.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895, once called Roentgen rays.

clue.text: Dainty morsel songbird pecked

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
bit means pecked, nipped with the beak

explanation.surface: A songbird pecks at a tasty scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small choice piece of food, a delicacy.

clue.text: Bar employee from quietly dividing sample

indicators.note: dividing means splitting a word, so the letter goes inside it

parts.note: a taster is a small sample
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A barman quietly splits a sample of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster draws drinks from the tap, so is someone working behind a bar.

clue.text: Linguist in college gained first in Latin internally

parts.note: a poly is a polytechnic college

indicators.note: internally means inside, so the letter goes within the other word

parts.note: got means gained

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A college student comes first in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot speaks many languages, a type of linguist.

clue.text: Oriental national oddly having only one name

indicators.note: oddly means strangely, so the letters are rearranged
N is name, and the fodder has two, so one is dropped

explanation.surface: A foreigner, oddly enough, goes by a single name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Laotian is a native of Laos in South-East Asia, so an Oriental in the old sense.

clue.text: Try one's hardest to identify breed

definitions.meaning: a variety or breed of animal or plant

explanation.definitionFit: Strain means both to exert oneself fully and a genetic line, two distinct senses.

clue.text: Playwright eats half the game and all the fowl

indicators.note: eats means takes in, so the playwright surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Joe Orton was an English playwright

indicators.note: half says only one of the two halves is kept

parts.note: ping-pong is a name for table tennis

explanation.surface: A dramatist devours half the game bird and then all of the chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests game birds, picking up 'fowl', but it is table tennis. An Orpington is a breed of chicken named after a town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orpington is a breed of domestic chicken, a heavy English fowl.

clue.text: Moving crowd acted like Mr Toad

definitions.meaning: a herd or crowd moving along
Mr Toad in The Wind in the Willows is a reckless motorist

explanation.definitionFit: Drove is a noun for a moving herd and the past tense of drive, as Toad drove cars.

clue.text: Material sea's thrown up around province

indicators.note: around places the reversed sea on either side of the province
in a down entry, throwing a word up reads it bottom to top

parts.note: Med is the Mediterranean Sea; the 's is a link
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

explanation.surface: Rough seas break around the coast of Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a sturdy cotton twill fabric, a material.

clue.text: Material volunteers turned over in soil

indicators.note: turned over in means the letters inside the word are flipped round

parts.note: to soil is to stain
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers dig over the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soil' looks like earth but is a verb meaning to dirty; 'turned over in' flips the volunteers' letters inside it, making AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth glossy fabric, a material.

clue.text: Bloke in berthing area rejecting married state

indicators.note: in places the bloke inside the other letters
rejecting means throwing out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a marina is where boats berth
a gent is a man, a bloke

explanation.surface: A man at a marina turns his back on married life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like marital state but is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a country, a sovereign state of South America.

clue.text: Caught fish immediately after drawing

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a ray is a flat fish
on means immediately after, as in 'on arrival'

explanation.surface: Someone catches a fish straight after sketching.
explanation.definitionFit: Crayon can mean a drawing done in crayon, as well as the stick itself.

clue.text: Dissenters mostly having to accept explosive candidate

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the other letters go inside
mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the noes are those voting against
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Opponents are forced to accept a candidate who might blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward for office, a candidate.
